packet.headline_seed: Rescuers search rubble for survivors as Venezuela earthquakes kill at least 188
packet.description_seed: Nearly 1,500 people have been injured after two seven-plus magnitude shallow quakes hit seconds apart.

what: Rescuers search rubble for survivors as Venezuela earthquakes kill at least 188

clean_source_blocks.text: Nearly 1,500 people have been injured after two seven-plus magnitude shallow quakes hit seconds apart.

We're pausing our live coverage for now, but you can read more in our online article here At least 188 people have been killed and more than 1,500 injured after powerful back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela, according to the latest reports Rescuers are searching the rubble in Caracas and the state of La Guaira, where the UN says more than 100 buildings have collapsed - video shows people running for cover The quakes, with magnitudes of 7.2 and 7.5, hit a minute apart. The second was the strongest to hit Venezuela since 1900 - you can see a "shake-map" here One man in Caracas says it felt like "the world was moving for a long time", while Leander tells the BBC he slept on the street after his home was damaged in the quakes

The earthquakes struck at 18:04 local time (22:04 GMT) on Wednesday - a national holiday in Venezuela, meaning more people would have been at home than on a normal weekday. Both quakes were shallow - the first centred 20.3km below the surface and the second at a depth of 10km, according to USGS. Jorge Rodríguez, the president of Venezuela's National Assembly, reported on Thursday that the death toll had risen, after the country's interim President Delcy Rodríguez declared a state of emergency. Several countries have pledged to help the rescue efforts, with the US promising $150m (£113m) in aid. What we know so far as rescuers race to find survivors 'I thought I was going to die' - Venezuelans describe earthquake panic

Watch: Moment earthquake hits Venezuela and leaves buildings collapsed Rescuers are searching through rubble in a rush to save lives after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela near the capital, killing at least 188 people and injuring more than 1,500. In Caracas and the nearby coastal city of La Guaira, people could be heard calling for help from under the debris of collapsed buildings. The first 7.2-magnitude quake was followed seconds later by an even stronger 7.5-magnitude one, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS), with both occurring close to the surface, making destruction more severe. Many more people are feared dead, with others left homeless or too afraid to stay in damaged, unsafe buildings sleeping in the streets after the disaster.

Rescuers are searching through rubble in a rush to save lives after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela near the capital, killing at least 188 people and injuring more than 1,500.

In Caracas and the nearby coastal city of La Guaira, people could be heard calling for help from under the debris of collapsed buildings.

The first 7.2-magnitude quake was followed seconds later by an even stronger 7.5-magnitude one, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS), with both occurring close to the surface, making destruction more severe.

Many more people are feared dead, with others left homeless or too afraid to stay in damaged, unsafe buildings sleeping in the streets after the disaster.

Both quakes were shallow - the first centred 20.3km below the surface and the second at a depth of 10km, according to USGS.

Jorge Rodríguez, the president of Venezuela's National Assembly, reported on Thursday that the death toll had risen, after the country's interim President Delcy Rodríguez declared a state of emergency.

Several countries have pledged to help the rescue efforts, with the US promising $150m (£113m) in aid.

What we know so far as rescuers race to find survivors

'I thought I was going to die' - Venezuelans describe earthquake panic

Jorge Rodríguez said 250 buildings had been damaged or lost, mostly in La Guaira, where the BBC verified footage of a 10-storey hotel reduced to rubble. On Thursday, people were searching for loved ones there.

Juan Ortiz told the BBC one of his close friends had been confirmed dead, another was believed to be under the rubble, and around 20 people he knew who live in the coastal area were missing.

Mayor Gustavo Duque of Chacao, which forms part of the greater metropolitan area of Caracas, said outside one ruined building on Thursday that 11 people had died there and 23 had been rescued.

payload.title: Venezuelassa etsitään eloonjääneitä raunioista voimakkaiden maanjäristysten jälkeen
payload.summary: Venezuelassa ainakin 188 ihmistä on kuollut ja yli 1 500 loukkaantunut kahdessa voimakkaassa maanjäristyksessä. Pelastustyöt jatkuvat Caracasissa ja La Guairassa, missä rakennuksia on sortunut.
payload.content:
Venezuelassa pelastajat etsivät eloonjääneitä raunioista kahden voimakkaan maanjäristyksen jälkeen. Ainakin 188 ihmistä on kuollut ja yli 1 500 loukkaantunut, kun kaksi matalaa ja yli seitsemän magnitudin järistystä iski maahan lyhyen ajan sisällä keskiviikkona.

## Pelastajat etsivät ihmisiä sortuneista rakennuksista

Pelastustöitä on tehty erityisesti pääkaupunki Caracasissa ja La Guairan osavaltiossa. Tietojen mukaan ihmiset ovat huutaneet apua sortuneiden rakennusten alta Caracasissa ja läheisessä rannikkokaupunki La Guairassa.

YK:n mukaan yli sata rakennusta on romahtanut. Monien pelätään edelleen olevan kateissa tai kuolleita, ja osa asukkaista on jäänyt kodittomiksi. Toiset eivät ole uskaltaneet palata vaurioituneisiin rakennuksiin, vaan ovat nukkuneet kaduilla järistysten jälkeen.

Yksi Caracasissa ollut mies kuvasi kokemusta sanomalla, että tuntui kuin ”maailma olisi liikkunut pitkään”. Eräs toinen asukas kertoi nukkuneensa kadulla sen jälkeen, kun hänen kotinsa vaurioitui.

## Kaksi voimakasta järistystä iski lähellä pintaa

Järistykset tapahtuivat keskiviikkona kello 18.04 paikallista aikaa, eli kello 22.04 GMT-aikaa. Päivä oli Venezuelassa kansallinen vapaapäivä, minkä vuoksi tavallista useampi ihminen on voinut olla kotona järistysten aikaan.

Yhdysvaltain geologisen tutkimuskeskuksen USGS:n mukaan ensimmäisen järistyksen magnitudi oli 7,2 ja toisen 7,5. Ne tapahtuivat hyvin lähellä maanpintaa: ensimmäisen keskus oli 20,3 kilometrin syvyydessä ja toisen 10 kilometrin syvyydessä. Matalat järistykset voivat aiheuttaa laajempaa tuhoa, koska niiden energia välittyy voimakkaammin maan pinnalle.

Toinen järistys oli tietojen mukaan voimakkain Venezuelassa sitten vuoden 1900. Järistykset seurasivat toisiaan vain lyhyellä viiveellä.

## Hätätila julistettu ja apua luvattu

Venezuelan kansalliskokouksen puheenjohtaja Jorge Rodríguez kertoi torstaina kuolonuhrien määrän nousseen. Maan väliaikainen presidentti Delcy Rodríguez on julistanut hätätilan.

Useat maat ovat luvanneet tukea pelastustoimiin. Yhdysvallat on ilmoittanut lupaavansa 150 miljoonan dollarin, eli noin 113 miljoonan punnan, avun. Pelastustyöt jatkuvat samalla, kun viranomaiset yrittävät arvioida tuhojen laajuutta ja tavoittaa raunioihin mahdollisesti jääneitä ihmisiä.

Kaksi voimakasta, matalaa järistystä iski keskiviikkona lyhyen ajan sisällä.
Pelastajat etsivät eloonjääneitä raunioista Caracasissa ja La Guairassa.

Nearly 1,500 people have been injured after two seven-plus magnitude shallow quakes hit seconds apart.

We're pausing our live coverage for now, but you can read more in our online article here At least 188 people have been killed and more than 1,500 injured after powerful back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela, according to the latest reports Rescuers are searching the rubble in Caracas and the state of La Guaira, where the UN says more than 100 buildings have collapsed - video shows people running for cover The quakes, with magnitudes of 7.2 and 7.5, hit a minute apart. The second was the strongest to hit Venezuela since 1900 - you can see a "shake-map" here One man in Caracas says it felt like "the world was moving for a long time", while Leander tells the BBC he slept on the street after his home was damaged in the quakes

The earthquakes struck at 18:04 local time (22:04 GMT) on Wednesday - a national holiday in Venezuela, meaning more people would have been at home than on a normal weekday. Both quakes were shallow - the first centred 20.3km below the surface and the second at a depth of 10km, according to USGS. Jorge Rodríguez, the president of Venezuela's National Assembly, reported on Thursday that the death toll had risen, after the country's interim President Delcy Rodríguez declared a state of emergency. Several countries have pledged to help the rescue efforts, with the US promising $150m (£113m) in aid. What we know so far as rescuers race to find survivors 'I thought I was going to die' - Venezuelans describe earthquake panic

Watch: Moment earthquake hits Venezuela and leaves buildings collapsed Rescuers are searching through rubble in a rush to save lives after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela near the capital, killing at least 188 people and injuring more than 1,500. In Caracas and the nearby coastal city of La Guaira, people could be heard calling for help from under the debris of collapsed buildings. The first 7.2-magnitude quake was followed seconds later by an even stronger 7.5-magnitude one, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS), with both occurring close to the surface, making destruction more severe. Many more people are feared dead, with others left homeless or too afraid to stay in damaged, unsafe buildings sleeping in the streets after the disaster.
